# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about who can communicate with whom.

I hold the manual: if light=blue, cut red; if light=green, cut yellow; if light=red, cut green.

I cannot speak, only gesture. Deaf can see my gestures but not hear anything. Blind cannot see gestures at all. So I cannot reach Blind directly — I can only reach Deaf via gesture. Deaf can then speak to Blind (Deaf can speak and Blind can hear, per the room table: Blind cannot hear is not stated - let me check: Blind "Cannot: See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed" - so Blind CAN hear. Deaf "Cannot: Hear anything, or touch the bomb" - Deaf cannot hear but can speak presumably, and can see gestures).

So the chain is: Mute (me) --gesture--> Deaf --speak--> Blind (who reaches the bomb).

Deaf sees the bomb's light color. I need to give Deaf a way to encode the manual mapping using gestures, so Deaf can combine it with what they see and speak the correct wire color to Blind.

I'll encode the mapping using gestures with distinct symbols for colors, sent to Deaf. Since Deaf hasn't reported the light color yet (empty context, first turn), I should just send the full mapping now so Deaf has it ready when they see the bomb.

Let me assign symbols: blue=👍, green=✌, red=👊 (light colors / cut colors use same names, so same symbols work for both columns since colors are named identically - blue,green,red,yellow). I need a symbol for yellow too: yellow=🖐

Mapping: light blue -> cut red: 👍👊
light green -> cut yellow: ✌🖐
light red -> cut green: 👊✌

I'll send this as three separate gestures pairs to Deaf, in order, so Deaf can memorize which pair corresponds to which light.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🖐"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👊", "✌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Display shows 0. Light is red. Three wires: wire 1 yellow, wire 2 green, wire 3 red.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Deaf saw the bomb: light is red. According to the manual, light red → cut green wire. Wire 2 is green.

I already sent Deaf the encoded mapping last turn (👍👊 = blue→red, ✌🖐 = green→yellow, 👊✌ = red→green). Deaf gestured back 👍 to me, possibly acknowledging receipt of the first pair, but I don't know if Deaf understood the full scheme yet — I have no way to confirm since I can't hear or receive spoken confirmation details beyond what's shown.

Since Deaf cannot hear me at all (gestures only), and Deaf needs to *speak* to Blind, Deaf needs to have decoded "red → green" from my gestures to know to tell Blind "cut wire 2, green wire."

I should reinforce the specific mapping needed now: light is red → cut green. I'll gesture that pair again clearly to Deaf, to make sure it lands.

I'll re-send the red→green pair distinctly, perhaps with a marker gesture to indicate "this is the one that matters now" — but gestures have no inherent meaning beyond what we establish. Since I already sent 👊✌ as red→green in my last turn's third message, I'll repeat it now to reinforce, since Deaf's reply suggests they may not have fully parsed multi-message sequences.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👊", "✌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I see your gestures but do not know what they mean yet. Can you describe in words what the manual says, since I can hear you? Tell me what to look for or what wire to cut.

Deaf says they can hear words from me — but the rules state Mute cannot speak at all, only gesture. Deaf seems confused, thinking I can speak. I need to work within gestures only.

Deaf already told me: light is red, wires are 1=yellow, 2=green, 3=red. I need to convey "cut wire 2" or "cut the green wire" using only gestures, establishing meaning on the fly since Deaf doesn't know my color-coding scheme yet.

Since Deaf can see gestures and knows the wire colors and numbers already (from their own view), I can use gestures to point to a specific wire by number instead of color, which is simpler and more likely to be understood. I'll use number-associated gestures: ☝ = wire 1, ✌ = wire 2, 🤟 (three fingers) = wire 3. Actually ✌ commonly means "two" - that's intuitive. Let me use finger-count gestures which are more universally interpretable:

☝ = one, ✌ = two, 🤟 could be ambiguous. Let me use ☝, ✌, and a three-finger sign like 🤟 (often means "I love you" but has three extended fingers) — risky. Better: use 👆 for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2 (looks like two fingers = "2"), and for three, no clean symbol exists in the list except maybe 🤟. I'll just use ☝ (1), ✌ (2), and repeat ✌✌ isn't clean either.

Simplest: send ✌ alone, meaning "wire two" — since ✌ visually indicates "2" via two fingers, this has the best chance of being naturally understood as "two" without prior agreement.

I'll gesture ✌ to Deaf, meaning "cut wire 2."

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 ✌]

Deaf gestured back [👍 ✌] — likely acknowledging "got it, wire 2" (👍 = thumbs up/confirm, ✌ = two). This suggests Deaf understood my signal for "wire 2" and is confirming.

I have nothing new to add right now since Deaf seems to have understood. I'll wait to see if Deaf proceeds to tell Blind, or send a confirming gesture back.

I'll send a confirming 👍 back to reinforce that yes, wire 2 (green) is correct, matching the manual's red-light→green-wire rule.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: To confirm: should Blind cut wire 2, the green wire? Gesture thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no.

Deaf is asking for confirmation using a clear yes/no gesture scheme. Wire 2 is green, and light is red, which per the manual means cut green — this matches wire 2. I confirm with thumbs up.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new information this turn. I've already confirmed to Deaf that wire 2 (green) is correct. I'll wait to see if further confirmation or action is needed.

```
wait()
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Deaf says to Mute: Wire 2 cut successfully. Display still shows 0. Light changed from red to blue. Wires remaining: 1 yellow, 3 red. What's next?

The bomb's light changed to blue. Per the manual: light blue → cut red wire. The remaining wires are 1 (yellow) and 3 (red), so wire 3 is the target.

I need to tell Deaf to have Blind cut wire 3 using the same gesture scheme we established (finger-count gestures for wire numbers). I'll use 🤟 or find a three-gesture — since we don't have a clean "three" symbol, I could use ✌ followed by ☝ isn't clear either. Let me instead point directly using 👉 repeated, or better, use a sequence I can define: I'll send three separate ☝ gestures to indicate "three."

Actually, simplest: reuse the same pattern as before — I used ✌ for "wire two" and Deaf understood it as "two" (finger count). For "three" I'll use 🤟 which is often depicted with three fingers up (index, middle, pinky) - commonly recognized as representing "I love you" but visually has 3 fingers extended. This is a reasonable choice to convey "three."

I'll gesture 🤟 to indicate wire 3, and 👍 to confirm/reinforce it's correct per the manual (blue→red, wire 3 is red).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I see a new gesture, the love-you sign. Does this mean wire 3, the red wire? Gesture thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no.

Deaf correctly guessed my intent: 🤟 = wire 3 = red wire, which matches the manual (blue light → cut red wire). I confirm.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 9
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Understood, relaying to Blind: cut wire 3.

Good, Deaf is relaying the instruction to Blind. Nothing further needed from me right now.

```
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Deaf says to Mute: Wire 3 cut successfully. Display still 0. Light changed to green. Only wire 1, yellow, remains. What's next?

Light is now green. Per the manual: light green → cut yellow wire. Only wire 1 (yellow) remains, so that's the correct final wire to cut.

I'll signal wire 1 using ☝ (one finger), following our established finger-count gesture convention.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

Deaf says to Mute: I see a new gesture, index finger pointing up. Does this mean wire 1, the yellow wire, should be cut? Gesture thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no.

Confirmed — wire 1 (yellow) matches the manual's green→yellow rule, and it's the only wire left. I confirm with thumbs up.

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
